title: Riverfront music from sailors and the Brunus band on the balcony
summary: Mrs. Brunies describes foreign sailors playing on ships along the river and the Brunies family band entertaining the neighbourhood from the balcony.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: The beautiful music on the streets. Yeah. On the riverfront. Yeah.
What kind of music was on the riverfront?
Well, it just, it just, just like you see those men playing now, they have a band that comes on now. What is that band? The Polish band that comes on?
Oh. On Charlie and Gene.
Huh? It, I can't call it our band. But, uh, they play exactly like that riverfront.
Those are fine musicians.
That, that Polish band, it comes on Channel 13.
Oh.
Oh.
I can't remember.
They used all the different instruments then, did they? They used cardines. Cardines. Cardines.
Cardines.

But, uh, planets and banjos. They weren't educated men, most of them, but they, it was beautiful. There'd be one ship on top of the other there, you know, docked. And they played beautiful music. It was just as good as going to a, to a concert.
It would be the sailors that came in.

Sailors and the Norwegians and Danes. All the foreigners. All the foreigners, you know, but beautiful music. Beautiful. Really beautiful music. And then, of course, we had the Brunus band entertain us too, you know. Oh, sure. So we really didn't have to go too far, did we? How often? Because all you had was the Nickelodeums in those days, you know. You didn't have the nice plays.
How often did the Brunus band play there on the balcony?
Whenever the father wanted them to.

About once a week. About a couple of whiskers in them, and he had it all over. It would be about every once a week or two or three times a week? Every time I saw him pulling that fiddle, he, shh, shh, that whistle. He's whistling and all the boys come running. Yeah.
They're a good family.
Yes, they must have been.
Yes, you are. Let's see if I was a neighbor next to him, it would have been a noisy family.
